patches.old:
The building work ended that day, but the tower was not completed, for more was still to be built. There was a pause in the building. The six men ordered all the builders to withdraw for a little while and rest, but told the virgins not to leave the tower. It seemed to me that the virgins had been left to guard it.[a]

2. After everyone had withdrawn to rest, I said to the shepherd, “Sir, why was the tower’s building not completed?” He said, “The tower cannot yet be completed unless its lord comes and tests this building, so that he may replace any stones found unsound. The tower is being built according to his will.”[b]

3. “Sir,” I said, “I would like to know what this building of the tower means, and about the rock, the gate, the mountains, the virgins, and the stones that rose from the depth and went into the building without being cut.”[c]

4. “Why were ten stones put into the foundations first, then twenty-five, then thirty-five, then forty? And what about the stones that went into the building, were removed again and put back in their own place? Put my soul at rest about all these things, sir, and explain them to me.”[d]

5. “If your eagerness is not empty,” he said, “you will know everything. For in a few days we will come here, and you will see what else happens to this tower. You will understand all the parables exactly.”[e]

6. After a few days we came to the place where we had sat. He said to me, “Let us go to the tower, for the owner of the tower is coming to inspect it.” We went to the tower, and there was no one at all beside it except the virgins.

7. The shepherd asked the virgins whether the master of the tower had arrived. They said he was about to come and inspect the building.

  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “More” represents the continuing building; the working Greek has bracketed “again.” Its “all”
      builders and the paragraph2 repeated “and rest” are also bracketed. Michigan partly preserves paragraph1,
      ending within the guarding sentence; its extant text cannot certify the later inspection dialogue.
      The distinction between ending that day’s work and completing the tower remains explicit.
  - marker: b
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The tower’s lord/owner/master is distinguished from “sir,” Hermas’s respectful address to the
      shepherd. The draft retains the lord’s inspection and power to replace unsound stones without adding
      a named modern office or procedure.
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “Without being cut” is explicit here in the working Greek, unlike the supplied negative at S.
      9.iii.3. It gives an internal reason for provisionally retaining that conjecture, but does not make
      its negative a preserved word in Michigan or the other earlier witnesses.
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The question repeats the working sequence ten, twenty-five, thirty-five and forty. At this twenty-five
      the 1891 apparatus again reports Athos twenty and Ethiopic fifteen; the alternatives are the same
      substitutions in Hermas’s question. These counts are not harmonized by pretending that the witnesses
      agree.
  - marker: e
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “If your eagerness is not empty” renders kenospoudos without turning the condition into an unconditional
      promise. A long bar-marked version-supported supplement begins at “we will come here,” includes
      the explanation promise, and ends after the next paragraph’s “After a few days.” It is absent from
      Athos as reported. Without the supplement, the shorter sequence runs from “For after a few days”
      to “we came to the place where we had sat.” Michigan has already ended and does not fill this passage.

    virgins to stay at the tower. It seemed to me that the virgins had been left to guard it.[a]


    2. After everyone left to rest, I asked the shepherd, “Sir, why was the tower’s building not finished?”
    He said, “It cannot be finished until its lord comes to test it. He must replace any unsound stones
    he finds. The tower is being built according to his will.”[b]


    3. I said, “Sir, I want to understand this building of the tower. What about the rock, the gate, the
    mountains and the virgins? What about the stones that rose from the depth and went into the building
    without being cut?”[c]


    4. “Why were ten stones put into the foundations first, then twenty-five, thirty-five and forty? What
    about the stones that were used, then removed and put back where they came from? Put my soul at rest,
    sir. Explain all these things.”[d]


    5. He said, “If your eagerness is not empty, you will understand everything. In a few days we will
    come here. You will see what else happens to the tower and understand all the parables exactly.”[e]


    6. A few days later we came to where we had sat. He told me, “Let us go to the tower. Its owner is
    coming to inspect it.” We went there. Only the virgins were beside it.


    7. The shepherd asked the virgins if the tower’s master had arrived. They said he was about to come
    and inspect the building.'

      ending within the guarding sentence; its extant text cannot certify the later inspection dialogue.
      The distinction between ending that day’s work and completing the tower remains explicit.
  - marker: b
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The tower’s lord/owner/master is distinguished from “sir,” Hermas’s respectful address to the
      shepherd. The draft retains the lord’s inspection and power to replace unsound stones without adding
      a named modern office or procedure.
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “Without being cut” is explicit here in the working Greek, unlike the supplied negative at S.
      9.iii.3. It gives an internal reason for provisionally retaining that conjecture, but does not make
      its negative a preserved word in Michigan or the other earlier witnesses.
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The question repeats the working sequence ten, twenty-five, thirty-five and forty. At this twenty-five
      the 1891 apparatus again reports Athos twenty and Ethiopic fifteen; the alternatives are the same
      substitutions in Hermas’s question. These counts are not harmonized by pretending that the witnesses
      agree.
  - marker: e
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “If your eagerness is not empty” renders kenospoudos without turning the condition into an unconditional
      promise. A long bar-marked version-supported supplement begins at “we will come here,” includes
      the explanation promise, and ends after the next paragraph’s “After a few days.” It is absent from
      Athos as reported. Without the supplement, the shorter sequence runs from “For after a few days”
      to “we came to the place where we had sat.” Michigan has already ended and does not fill this passage.

  text: 'The building work ended that day, but the tower was not completed, for more was still to be built.
    There was a pause in the building. The six men ordered all the builders to withdraw for a little while
    and rest, but told the virgins not to leave the tower. It seemed to me that the virgins had been left
    to guard it.[a]


    2. After everyone had withdrawn to rest, I said to the shepherd, “Sir, why was the tower’s building
    not completed?” He said, “The tower cannot yet be completed unless its lord comes and tests this building,
    so that he may replace any stones found unsound. The tower is being built according to his will.”[b]


    3. “Sir,” I said, “I would like to know what this building of the tower means, and about the rock,
    the gate, the mountains, the virgins, and the stones that rose from the depth and went into the building
    without being cut.”[c]


    4. “Why were ten stones put into the foundations first, then twenty-five, then thirty-five, then forty?
    And what about the stones that went into the building, were removed again and put back in their own
    place? Put my soul at rest about all these things, sir, and explain them to me.”[d]


    5. “If your eagerness is not empty,” he said, “you will know everything. For in a few days we will
    come here, and you will see what else happens to this tower. You will understand all the parables
    exactly.”[e]


    6. After a few days we came to the place where we had sat. He said to me, “Let us go to the tower,
    for the owner of the tower is coming to inspect it.” We went to the tower, and there was no one at
    all beside it except the virgins.


    7. The shepherd asked the virgins whether the master of the tower had arrived. They said he was about
    to come and inspect the building.'
